passages.scripture: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?

lines.text: You experience conflicts among yourselves.
You experience quarrels among yourselves.
These conflicts have a cause.
Your own desires cause these conflicts.
Your desires fight within your bodies.
Your passions wage war inside you.
These inner battles lead to your disputes.

passages.scripture: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.

lines.text: James addresses Christians who experience conflict and desire.
You want things you do not have.
You desire and cannot obtain.
You are jealous of others.
You even kill to get what you want.
Or you kill in your heart by being hateful to get what you want.
You quarrel with each other.
You fight among yourselves.
And yet you still do not have what you desire.
One reason you do not have something is because you do not ask God for it.

passages.scripture: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.

lines.text: You asked God for things.
But you did not receive what you ask for.
You did not receive, because you asked with wrong motives.
You want to spend what you receive on your own pleasures.

passages.scripture: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.

lines.text: Some people have committed adultery against God.
They are adulteresses.
These people are unfaithful to God.
They did not love God as their Husband.
Instead, they committed adultery with God.
They loved the world instead of God.
Friendship with the world means hostility toward God.
Anyone who chooses to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.

passages.scripture: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?

lines.text: God caused His Spirit to live in us.
The Spirit inside us deeply desires us.
The Spirit yearns for us with jealousy.
The Spirit yearns for our affections.
The Spirit deeply desires us to love God above all else.
Scripture does not speak for no reason.
Do not think the Scripture speaks in vain.
Scripture says the Spirit longs for us with jealousy.

passages.scripture: But He gives us more grace. This is why it says: “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

lines.text: God gives us more grace.
God opposes proud people.
God gives grace to humble people.

passages.scripture: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

lines.text: God is the Lord.
God is powerful.
Submit yourselves to God.
The devil is your enemy.
Resist the devil.
The devil will flee from you.

passages.scripture: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.

lines.text: God is holy.
God wants people to come close to Him.
Draw near to God.
God will draw near to you.
If you sin, then cleanse your hands.
If you are double-minded, then purify your hearts.

passages.scripture: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.

lines.text: James addresses Christians who have sinned and are double-minded.
James commands them to grieve.
James commands them to mourn.
James commands them to weep.
James tells them to turn their laughter into mourning.
James tells them to turn their joy into gloom.

passages.scripture: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.

lines.text: The Lord is powerful and holy.
You must humble yourselves before the Lord.
If you humble yourself before Him, He will lift you up.
The Lord will exalt you.

passages.scripture: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.

lines.text: Brothers, do not slander each other.
If you speak against your brother, then you speak against the law.
If you speak against your brother, then you judge the law.
If you judge your brother, then you speak against the law.
If you judge your brother, then you judge the law.
If you judge the law, then you are not a doer of the law.
Instead being a doer of the law, if you judge the law, then you become a judge of the law.

passages.scripture: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

lines.text: God is the only Lawgiver.
God is the only Judge.
God alone has the power to save.
God alone has the power to destroy.
You are not the Judge of your neighbor.
You do not have the right to judge your neighbor.

passages.scripture: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”

lines.text: James addresses people who make plans without considering God.
He speaks to those who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city.”
These people plan to spend a year in that city.
They intend to do business there.
And they expect to make a profit.

passages.scripture: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.

lines.text: You do not know what will happen tomorrow.
You cannot see the future.
Your life is short.
Your life is like a mist.
A mist appears for a little while.
Then the mist disappears.
Your life is like that mist.
Your life is only here for a short time.
Then your life is gone.

passages.scripture: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”

lines.text: You should not speak with certainty about your plans for the future.
You do not believe that you can predict the future.
You should say, “If the Lord is willing, we will be alive.”
You should also say, “If the Lord is willing, we will do this or that.”

passages.scripture: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.

lines.text: If you speak improperly about the future, you boast in your proud intentions.
This boasting comes from arrogance.
All such boasting is evil.

passages.scripture: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.

lines.text: A person may know what is right.
This person understands what is good to do.
If this person does not do what is right, he sins.
Not doing the good you know you need to do is sin.
